title: Northbridge Medical - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Redwood onboarding. Covered goals, timeline, technical prerequisites (VPC, SSO, KMS), initial pilot scope, roles, and next steps. Customer asked about SOC 2, data residency, and latency/cost tradeoffs. SE to run initial benchmark and CSM to schedule weekly check-ins.
topics: Pilot scope: inference workload and success metrics
next_steps: Jordan to send SOW and onboarding timeline (by 2026-04-06)
Priya to schedule technical deep-dive for benchmarking (by 2026-04-08)
Customer to share sample data/queries for pilot (by 2026-04-09)
CSM Carlos to set up weekly 30-min check-ins starting 2026-04-13

header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood CSM); Dr. Elena Ruiz (Northbridge CTO), Mark Chen (Head of Engineering), Aisha Khan (DevOps), Samir Patel (Security), Lena Ortiz (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood - I'm the account lead. Priya is our solutions engineer and Carlos from customer success will run the onboarding cadence. Uh, can you each do a quick intro?
[00:12] Elena: Sure. Elena Ruiz, CTO at Northbridge. We're excited to get Redwood running for our clinical triage models.
[00:18] Mark: Mark Chen, head of eng. I'll be leading integration.
[00:22] Aisha: Aisha, DevOps. I'll handle the VPC/peering stuff.
[00:26] Samir: Samir, security. I'll be the compliance point.
[00:30] Jordan: Awesome. Ok, agenda - quick goals, timeline, tech prerequisites like VPC, SSO, KMS, then pilot scope and next steps.
[00:38] Priya: Hi all - I'll cover the infra and perf checklist and what we usually see during pilot. Note: transcription might show some words weirdly, e.g., KV cache sometimes becomes "KV cash" in auto-transcripts, so sorry in advance for typos.
[00:48] Jordan: First, goals from Northbridge's side? Elena?
[00:52] Elena: Primary goal is to reduce triage time and improve consistency. We want model inference in our app with p95 latency under 400 ms for short prompts and cost under our current baseline. Pilot scope is 2 months to evaluate latency, throughput, and output quality.
[01:08] Jordan: Great. That's consistent with other health customers. Typical pilot: week 1-2 set up access + network, week 3-4 run benchmarks, week 5-8 integrate and run quality evals. We can tighten or loosen that depending on your team's availability.
[01:24] Mark: Sounds feasible. Aisha, any blockers on VPC peering?
[01:29] Aisha: We need the peering docs and IP ranges. Also want to confirm whether we do private deployment or dedicated. For now we prefer Redwood Dedicated if possible because of data isolation, but we want to see cost difference versus hosted.
[01:44] Priya: Quick note - Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation. Hosted is fastest to launch and cheaper for low volume. For Dedicated we can recommend autoscaling policies and burst pools. We'll run cost estimates in the SOW.
[01:57] Samir: On compliance - do you have SOC 2 and ISO reports? Also we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for all request metadata. Data residency is US only for us.
[02:11] Jordan: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated. Audit logging is available via the console and can be exported. I'll attach links in the follow-up.
[02:24] Elena: Good. Also timeline - we need production by end of Q2. That gives about 12 weeks. Is that realistic?
[02:33] Carlos: With a tight pilot and SE support, yes. We'll plan a two-week pilot and fast follow into pre-prod if benchmarks look good.
[02:40] Priya: For the technical deep-dive - I'll need sample payloads, average length, tokens per request, concurrency targets, and any special function calls or tool integrations you plan to use.
[02:52] Mark: We'll share a sample traffic file with typical prompt/response pairs and peak concurrency goals. Expect maybe 6-8 concurrent workers hitting the endpoint; some batches of longer context up to 2k tokens for extended notes.
[03:06] Priya: Great. For benchmarks I'll run hosted endpoints and a Dedicated sim to show p50/p95/p99 and token cost estimates. Note that quantization profiles can change memory and latency. We'll try a few configurations.
[03:18] Aisha: On networking - do you support VPC peering and private links? We prefer Private deployment or VPC peering to avoid public egress.
[03:28] Priya: Yes - we support VPC peering and Private deployments. There's also an option for outbound-only peering for the control plane; we'll document both. Sometimes the transcript mislabels it as V-P-C, but it's VPC.
[03:40] Samir: For key management - do you support customer KMS or HSM?
[03:45] Jordan: Customer KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated; HSM integrations available via our enterprise offering.
[03:52] Elena: Any note on data retention and log redaction? We need logs for debugging but with PIIs redacted.
[03:59] Carlos: Redwood has configurable retention and redaction settings. We'll share the security docs and a short runbook for redaction patterns.
[04:08] Jordan: Ok next, pilot success criteria - Elena?
[04:11] Elena: p95 latency under 400 ms for short prompts, 99% uptime during business hours, and parity or improvement on precision for triage decisions based on our evaluation set. Also cost per 1k tokens approximate target.
[04:23] Jordan: We'll capture those in the SOW and measurements.
[04:26] Priya: Practical infra checklist: (1) test account credentials - we'll need an API key and a test project; (2) VPC peering or Private endpoint details; (3) sample payloads; (4) expected concurrency; (5) list of stakeholders and weekly check-in invite.
[04:41] Mark: We'll give creds for a non-prod environment and a subset of the dataset.
[04:45] Aisha: On peering, we prefer to do it in the first week.
[04:49] Priya: Perfect. I'll add network steps to the runbook. Also note - if you want an on-prem package we can discuss but that usually extends timeline by several weeks for air-gapped installs.
[05:02] Elena: Not for the pilot. Maybe later.
[05:05] Samir: Can we talk about service level objectives and support - escalation path?
[05:10] Jordan: For Dedicated customers we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. Carlos will be your CSM for day-to-day and our support on-call for critical issues. We'll include the support tiers in the SOW.
[05:21] Priya: Quick technical question from our side - any specialized models or private models you'll bring, or are you planning to use Redwood-curated open models?
[05:31] Lena: We plan to use an internally fine-tuned model for triage; we'll need to upload that model artifact and request onboarding guidance.
[05:39] Priya: Uploads are supported for Private/Dedicated. For hosted we can host if model size fits our catalog constraints. We'll need the model family, weights format and any custom kernels. Sometimes transcripts mis-interpret "LLM weights" as "L-L-M weights" - just flagging.
[05:53] Elena: We'll share model details after we sign the SOW.
[05:57] Jordan: Great. Anything on integrations - are you using our webhooks, or do you need a plugin?
[06:03] Mark: Webhooks for async notifications, and we may use direct SDK for sync calls.
[06:09] Priya: Ok I'll document both patterns. For async large payloads we recommend callback flows.
[06:15] Jordan: Let's cover the ramp plan: week 0-1 network + access; week 2 perf run; week 3 integration tests; week 4-8 full pilot and evaluation. Can we confirm resource allocation from Northbridge?
[06:28] Elena: Yes - Mark and Aisha will lead engineering tasks, Samir for security sign-offs, and Lena for product QA.
[06:36] Carlos: I'll schedule weekly check-ins and a status doc in the shared folder.
[06:40] Jordan: Any immediate risks?
[06:42] Samir: Data residency and SOC2 - need those docs. Also, may need to route through our HSM for keys - can Redwood support that?
[06:52] Priya: We can integrate with customer KMS and some HSM flows. We'll validate the exact flow in the technical deep-dive.
[06:59] Jordan: Ok wrapping up - recap of next steps: Jordan send SOW and onboarding timeline; Priya schedule technical deep-dive and run benchmarks; Customer to send sample payloads and VPC details; Carlos schedule weekly check-ins.
[07:15] Mark: Sounds good. When will we get the SOC2?
[07:18] Jordan: I'll attach our SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary in the follow-up email today.
[07:23] Elena: One more thing - pricing for Dedicated vs hosted, can you give rough numbers now?
[07:28] Jordan: I'll include ballpark numbers in the SOW. For the pilot, we can provision a small Dedicated pool; we'll show token cost estimates and autoscale configs.
[07:38] Aisha: For networking, what's the typical peering lead time?
[07:41] Priya: Usually 2-3 business days once we have the IP ranges and contacts.
[07:46] Carlos: I'll send the calendar invites for weekly check-ins and a follow-up doc with links: SOC2, onboarding playbook, bench template, and the SOW draft.
[07:57] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Any final questions?
[07:59] Lena: No, thanks. Looking forward.
[08:01] Jordan: Great - talk soon.
[55:00] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., KV cache -> "KV cash", VPC -> "V-P-C"). Shared artifacts mentioned: link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2, doc: onboarding-playbook.md, sheet: benchmark-template.csv.
